title: Generation of human embryonic stem cell-derived lung organoids
protocol: Aspirate the medium from hESCs at 75%–85% confluency.
Wash hESCs with 2 mL of room temperature DPBS (without Ca2+/Mg2+) per well of a 6 well plate.
Aspirate the DPBS from the well.
Add 1 mL of room temperature Accutase containing Y-27632 (10 μM) per well.
Incubate cultures in a 37°C/5% CO2 cell culture incubator for 3–6 minutes to dissociate cells into single cells.
Check hESC colonies under the microscope after 3 minutes; cells should appear more refringent but not floating.
Aspirate Accutase solution carefully without disturbing the cells.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed mTeSR1TM with 10 μM Y-27632 per well into a 6-well plate.
Gently pipette up and down to detach cells from the well using a 1 mL tip.
Collect medium containing detached cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Add 6–12 mL of pre-warmed mTeSR1TM with 10 μM Y-27632 to cells.
Gently pipette up and down to ensure a homogeneous single cell solution.
Count cells using an automatic cell counter, excluding dead cells with trypan blue.
Seed cells at a density of 1.0–2.0 × 10^5 cells/cm² into Matrigel-coated wells using mTeSR1TM with 10 μM Y-27632 to achieve a final volume of 2 mL per well in a 6-well plate.
Gently move the plate back and forth and left to right several times to ensure an even distribution of the cell suspension.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C/5% CO₂ cell culture incubator overnight (12–16 h) to initiate differentiation into definitive endoderm cells.
Aspirate the medium from hESCs when confluency reaches 95% after overnight growth.
Wash hESCs with 2 mL of room temperature RPMI 1640 medium per well in a 6 well plate.
Aspirate the RPMI 1640 medium from the well.
Remove mTeSR1TM complete medium from hESCs.
Gently wash hESCs with room temperature RPMI 1640 medium.
Add 2 mL of definitive endoderm differentiation medium per well.
Incubate cultures at 37°C/5% CO2.
Replenish the definitive endoderm differentiation medium every 24 hours for 3 days.
Aspirate the medium from cultures on day 3.
Wash the cultures with 2 mL of room temperature RPMI 1640 medium per well.
Add 2 mL of anterior foregut endoderm differentiation medium per well.
Incubate cultures at 37°C/5% CO2.
Replenish the anterior foregut endoderm differentiation medium every 24 hours for 4 days.
Aspirate the medium from cultures on day 7.
Wash the cultures with 2 mL of room temperature DPBS (without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) per well.
Add 1 mL of room temperature Accutase containing Y-27632 (10 μM) per well.
Incubate cultures in 37°C/5% CO2 cell culture incubator for 2–4 minutes.
Check the cells under the microscope after 2 minutes.
Incubate cells with Accutase for 2-4 minutes, checking every 2 minutes under microscope.
Aspirate the Accutase carefully and add 1 mL of pre-warmed lung organoids differentiation medium with 10 μM Y-27632 per well in the 6 well plate.
Gently pipette up and down to detach cells from the well into the medium.
Collect the medium containing cells into a 1.5 mL sterile eppendorf tube.
Count cells using an automatic cell counter with trypan blue exclusion.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet, using a 20 μL tip to remove remaining supernatant.
Tap the cell pellet to ensure there are no clumps.
Place eppendorf tube on ice for 1-3 minutes.
Add 100-200 μl of ice-cold 3D Matrigel to cells and gently pipette up and down several times.
Thaw 3D Matrigel on ice overnight before use.
Place a 100 μL tip in the freezer to pre-chill.
Pipette 20–30 μL of 3D Matrigel using a cold pipette tip.
Plate the Matrigel droplets containing anterior foregut endoderm cells into a 6 well plate.
Place the plate on ice until the Matrigel solidifies.
Add 3–5 mL of pre-warmed lung organoids differentiation medium to each well, ensuring complete coverage of the Matrigel droplet.
Incubate cultures at 37°C/5% CO2 for 15–30 min until Matrigel droplets have solidified.
Replenish the lung organoids differentiation medium every 48–72 h for 34 days.
Re-embed organoids every 5–10 days, or sooner if necessary.
Check cultures every 2–3 days under the microscope.
Pick up the entire droplet containing organoids with a serum pipette and move it to a 1.5 mL sterile eppendorf tube.
Remove all media using 200 μL or 1 mL tips.
Centrifuge the cultures at 200 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Use a 20 μL tip to aspirate residual culture medium (30–80 μL typically).
Gently pipette up and down using a 20 μL tip to cut organoids and old Matrigel.
Place the mixture on ice for 1–2 minutes to cool it down before re-embedding.
Mechanically cut old 3D Matrigel droplets into small clumps using a 20 μL tip.
Gently pipette up and down with care to avoid creating bubbles during cutting.
Transfer 100–200 μL of ice-cold fresh 3D Matrigel to an eppendorf tube.
Mix the contents well in the eppendorf tube.
Place re-embedded organoids in a 6-well plate on ice.
Allow the plate to sit at room temperature for 15–30 minutes until Matrigel droplets solidify.
Add 3–5 mL of pre-warmed lung organoids differentiation medium per well, ensuring complete coverage over the Matrigel droplet.
Incubate cultures in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C/5% CO2.
Replenish the lung organoids differentiation medium every 48–72 hours.
Pipette with care to avoid making bubbles.
If there are bubbles, centrifuge the eppendorf tube at 200 g at 4°C for 5 min.
Remove bubbles with 200 μL tips.
Mix organoids and 3D Matrigel again to make an even distribution of organoids.
